analysis.title: U.S. Software: rAImo's AI Newsletter #132: Where Enterprise AI Still Falls Short
key_insights: Barclays says accuracy and consistency remain the main hurdles for enterprise AI. Model performance declines as tasks require reasoning across more complex or conflicting information, and getting the right answer once does not mean getting it consistently.

On MMEnterprise-Bench (KAIST and Korea University, 10 models, 1,613 questions on simulated workplace records), the best model, GPT-5.6, scores ~83% on single-text questions, ~52% on multiple-text questions and ~28% when multiple images are involved. Barclays says synthesizing across sources is a different challenge from understanding one item.

Proprietary models score ~62-77% on categories where the relevant information is readily available. On Cross-Source and Temporal questions, which involve conflicting or updated information, they fall to ~51% and ~54%.

Proprietary models reach ~74% accuracy on unanswerable questions, where the records do not support an answer. Barclays calls this a relative strength: models recognize missing evidence better than they reconcile conflicting evidence.

Feeding more context helps only partly. Raising retrieved records from 10 to 50 improved accuracy for all models tested, proprietary models most, but overall accuracy for the best model stayed below 70% even with 5x the data.

Mercor's APEX-Agents 1.1 shows a consistency gap of ~17-31ppt between tasks completed at least once in four attempts (Pass@4) and tasks completed in all four (Pass^4). Barclays says repeatability may matter as much as peak capability for enterprise use.

Barclays concludes that better model capability alone may not speed enterprise AI deployment. It supports a measured view on the pace of enterprise AI adoption and reinforces the potential advantage of incumbent software vendors that already sit on enterprise data and established workflows.
Barclays rates the U.S. Software industry view POSITIVE. CoreWeave (CRWV) is Equal Weight with a $105 price target, closing at $55.19 on 26-Oct-2026.

Other AI news listed: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.1 Terra with standard API prices 50% below GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol (10/26). OpenAI is bringing its models to Google's cloud, so they will be on all three top cloud providers (CNBC, 10/21). Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet, a proactive agent app (10/21). DeepSeek raised about 100 billion yuan ($14.98 billion) (Reuters, 10/22). IBM and NVIDIA expanded agent-security work around NVIDIA OpenShell (10/26).

market_movers.rationale: The $105 target applies ~33x CY27E EV/EBIT to CY27E EBIT of ~$4.19bn, reflecting strong RPO growth and higher sentiment for AI infrastructure software peers. The stock closed at $55.19 on 26-Oct-2026. The last target change was 12-Aug-2026, from $90 to $105.

sector_views.rationale: Barclays' industry view is Positive, meaning fundamentals and valuations are improving. The newsletter argues that incumbent vendors sitting on enterprise data and workflows keep an advantage while enterprise AI accuracy and consistency gaps persist.

risk_factors: Competition in AI-optimized IaaS could challenge CoreWeave's market-leading position.
Microsoft and other key customers are building competing solutions and could bring more AI IaaS in-house, hurting CoreWeave's growth outlook.
Global supply chain uncertainty could delay CoreWeave's capex and its ability to build out infrastructure for customers.

Benchmark results depend on the benchmark's retrieval and evaluation design. Barclays says they are a controlled test of enterprise-record reasoning, not a direct measure of production deployment performance.
charts_described: Figure 1 plots GPT-5.6 accuracy by question type (Single Text, Multiple Text, Single Image, Multiple Images, Text + Images) at k=10. The text cites ~83% for single text, ~52% for multiple text and ~28% for multiple images.
Figure 4 shows the Pass@4 versus Pass^4 gap: Claude Opus 5 31.0%, Claude Fable 5.1 28.7%, Grok 4.6 26.7%, GPT-6 Astra 17.0%.
geopolitical: DeepSeek's funding round has backing from state-linked and corporate investors as China aims to stay competitive in the AI race against the US (per the Reuters excerpt).

theme_stances.key_argument: Model accuracy falls on complex, conflicting or multi-source information and results are inconsistent across repeated attempts, so capability gains alone may not speed enterprise deployment.
theme_stances.evidence: improving model capabilities alone may not be enough to accelerate enterprise AI deployments

theme_stances.key_argument: Incumbent software vendors that already sit on enterprise data and established workflows may keep an advantage as AI adoption proceeds at a measured pace.
theme_stances.evidence: potential advantage of incumbent software vendors that already sit on top of enterprise data
